pages.text: A CONSTANT line makes a constant: a named value that never changes.

It looks like a VARIABLE line, but it must have a value. The value is a LITERAL, not a calculation and not another constant; lists, hashes and structs get theirs in a code block, like a VARIABLE. You can't ASSIGN to a constant, and it can't receive a CALL result.

Some constants exist in every program. The names of the errors, like $(1)DIVISION_BY_ZERO$(), hold their codes. $(1)COLOR_BLACK$() to $(1)COLOR_WHITE$() are the colors for COLOR. $(1)SHEET$() tells a program about its sheet: $(1)number$(), $(1)program$(), $(1)owner$() and the position $(1)x$(), $(1)y$(), $(1)z$() of its first floor block. $(1)PID$() tells it about its process: $(1)pid$(), $(1)program$(), $(1)function$(), $(1)owner$(), $(1)activator$() (the player who started it, empty for other redstone signals, mobs and timer blocks), the position $(1)x$(), $(1)y$(), $(1)z$() and $(1)dimension$() of the trigger block, $(1)debug$() and the tick it $(1)started$(). $(1)CURSOR$() tells it about its cursor right now: the $(1)line$(), the $(1)function$(), the $(1)depth$() of the calls, and how many slots of the stack are used ($(1)stack_used$()) of $(1)stack_size$(). Their types are SHEET_INFO, PID_INFO and CURSOR_INFO. $(1)C0DE_VERSION$() is the version of c0de as text, like "0.4.0". Other mods can add constants of their own, like $(1)C0DE_NET_VERSION$() of c0de net.
Craft a type base and three bones, or turn a VARIABLE block into a CONSTANT block.
$(1)CONSTANT BASE INTEGER 42$(br)CONSTANT ORIGIN STRUCT point$(br)BEGIN$(br)  x 3$(br)END CONSTANT$()
